definition: In artificial neural networks, a hybrid Kohonen self-organizing map is a type of self-organizing map (SOM) named for the Finnish professor Teuvo Kohonen, where the network architecture consists of an input layer fully connected to a 2–D SOM or Kohonen layer.
details: The output from the Kohonen layer, which is the winning neuron, feeds into a hidden layer and finally into an output layer. In other words, the Kohonen SOM is the front–end, while the hidden and output layer of a multilayer perceptron is the back–end of the hybrid Kohonen SOM. The hybrid Kohonen SOM was first applied to machine vision systems for image classification and recognition. Hybrid Kohonen SOM has been used in weather prediction and especially in forecasting stock prices, which has made a challenging task considerably easier. It is fast and efficient with less classification error, hence is a better predictor, when compared to Kohonen SOM and backpropagation networks.

explainer.lead: A hybrid Kohonen self-organizing map uses a Kohonen layer as a front end and a multilayer perceptron as a back end, combining unsupervised clustering with supervised output. It matters for tasks needing both topographic grouping and prediction.

tiers.eli5: It is like a sorting desk that first groups similar items, then passes each group to a specialist who makes the final call.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers feed inputs into a fully connected 2-D SOM, take the winning neuron, and pass it through hidden and output layers; the pitfall is that the unsupervised stage may discard detail the supervised stage needs, so the map size must be chosen carefully.
tiers.paperLevel: Architecture: an input layer fully connected to a 2-D Kohonen layer whose winning neuron feeds a hidden layer and then an output layer, i.e. SOM front end plus MLP back end. It was first applied to machine vision for image classification and recognition; performance depends on map size and training procedure.

explainer.example: Image features are mapped to a winning neuron in the Kohonen grid, and that neuron's index drives an MLP that outputs the image class.
